verdict_rationale: All six plan_review_v1 findings are resolved in plan_v2 and each resolution is verified against the live code, not merely the plan prose. F1 (MAJOR) is the load-bearing one: plan_v2 introduces a dedicated milestone M3 for a human-gated 'wf clear-invocation --by <human>' recovery that releases a confirmed-dead open_invocation, logs a distinct 'invocation_cleared' ledger event with actor 'human_recovery', refuses cleanly (exit non-zero, no state or ledger change) when no invocation is open, and touches no counters, pointers or freeze. Its test_R7 proves the exact deadlock is broken: 'wf transition ESCALATED' is FIRST refused by guard() with the open-invocation reason, then after clear-invocation the same ESCALATED transition succeeds. I re-confirmed the premise is real: guard() checks open_invocation at state.py line 252 and returns before the ESCALATED allowance at line 256, and PreToolUse single-flight blocks a new invocation at pretooluse_gate.py line 171, so an orphaned open_invocation genuinely deadlocks every exit until cleared. The R4/F1 closure wording no longer overclaims: M6, AC11 and the KNOWN_LIMITATIONS update enumerate exactly four mechanisms (init refusal, mid-run liveness re-check, 'wf accept' for stranded artifacts, 'wf clear-invocation' for orphaned invocations) and record the residual (--by is trusted not verified; the optional PreToolUse deny is deferred to the Security Reviewer; guard() ordering is intentionally left unchanged). No 'closed end-to-end' claim remains. F2: test placement is now self-consistent and monotonic, with matching cumulative counts in every verification block (M2 34 then 40 via test_R1..R6; M3 43 via test_R7..R9; M4 45 via test_R10..R11; M5 46 via test_R12); no milestone references a test introduced later. I verified the baseline is 34 tests OK and the arithmetic (34 plus 12 equals 46) holds. F3: the confirmed hook-sourced allowlist {invocation_requested, invocation_completed, invocation_failed} is baked into M4, AC8 and the assumptions with source lines, and 'artifact_accepted' is correctly excluded because the CLI writes it with actor='orchestrator' (state.py lines 484 to 486); I re-confirmed all four source lines. F4: the M1 core save/emit contract is now unambiguous: the core does not call save_state and emits no block or ok, with exactly ONE intentional exception, the _semantic integrity-hold branch (subagentstop_validate.py lines 160 to 171) which itself saves and logs 'integrity_violation' then 'verification' and is moved verbatim; the contradictory rerun_tests parameter is dropped so accept_artifact is (root, st, atype, version, *, actor=None) and _semantic keeps reading verify.rerun_tests from st. I confirmed those lines match. F5: 'wf accept' AND the new 'wf clear-invocation' are recorded as security-relevant surfaces in risks, scope.out, assumptions and security_observations, with compensating controls and the optional PreToolUse deny flagged (not adjudicated) to the Security Reviewer. F6: the previously untested claims now have named backing tests: AC3 fail-closed wrapper is pinned by test_R12 plus existing test_13; the expected()==None clean refusal by test_R6; and the cleared-open_invocation side effect of a successful 'wf accept' by test_R1 / AC4. Fresh adversarial pass: the test counts are arithmetically correct; no milestone is internally inconsistent; and clear-invocation does not create a silent ungoverned path (it requires --by, logs a distinct audited event, leaves PreToolUse single-flight governing the NEXT invocation, and its power to release the lock during a live run is exactly the residual already captured and routed to the Security Reviewer via F5). NON-BINDING implementor note (not a finding): the M1 adapter mapping moves the acceptance save_state to AFTER the in-core freeze and 'artifact_accepted' log, whereas today save_state (line 255) precedes freeze (line 256); on the happy path the on-disk result across state, registry and ledger is identical since they are independent files, and on the freeze-exception fault path both orderings are fail-closed (integrity_hold plus block via test_R12), so this is benign, but keep the happy-path end state byte-identical as the plan requires. Direction is correct and no blocker or major finding remains open; approving.

security_observations: Two Bash-callable authorities exceed 'wf approve': 'wf accept' advances current[atype], bumps counters and freezes; 'wf clear-invocation' releases the single-flight lock. Both are gated only by a trusted, unverified --by value; the optional PreToolUse deny while hooks show live is deferred. Routed to the Security Reviewer via F5.

'wf clear-invocation' during a genuinely live run could clear a legitimate open_invocation and open a window for a second concurrent invocation (single-flight escape). The plan captures this in risks[2] and defers the PreToolUse deny to the Security Reviewer; worth that review's explicit adjudication.

The extracted accept core still contains the shell=True test-rerun boundary and the git merge-base ancestry check; 'wf accept' makes both reachable from a human-run CLI entry point in addition to the hook. Same trust boundary as today, second entry point; worth the Security Reviewer's confirmation.
